Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The relevant methods getValues(String) and getValues(String, List) in CommandLineImpl delegate to getValues(Option, List) or getValues(Option). The one with just String calls getOption(trigger) to get the option and then calls the other getValues method with empty default values. The one with both String and List calls getOption(trigger) and calls getValues(Option, List) passing the default values list.

The current bug report indicates that defaults are only picked up if no arguments are passed in. In the test, option -b has argument with minimum 2, maximum 4, and 3 default values ["100", "1000", "10000"]. The command line args are "-b", "1", "2". The test expects getValues("-b") to return "[1, 2, 10000]" (the two given args plus the last default "10000").

From the initial investigation, the CommandLineImpl.getValues merely fetches values but probably relies on other components to fill argument defaults when the number of values is below maximum but above minimum.

The bug is likely in how the default values are added when there are some user arguments but fewer than the maximum number of arguments.

I will check the implementation of getValues(Option, List) to see how default values are merged with supplied values.

Therefore, I now want to see the source code of:

org.apache.commons.cli2.commandline.CommandLineImpl.getValues(org.apache.commons.cli2.Option, java.util.List)
